metadata.title: The Harvest
metadata.description: You wake in a stasis pod aboard a massive alien vessel. The Choir — eyeless bio-mechanical drones — are harvesters serving an ancient intelligence called The Convergence that consumes planets. Your pod malfunctioned. You're loose on a ship full of things that want you back in the jar. Below, a planet is being consumed alive.
metadata.author: ai-generated

setting.ambient_text: A subsonic hum vibrates through your bones. Amber fluid drains from your cracked pod, pooling on the organic-metallic floor. Bioluminescent veins pulse in the walls. Somewhere, something clicks — precise, mechanical, patient.

items.name: Stasis Fluid Vial
items.description: A vial of amber stasis fluid from your broken pod. The liquid shimmers faintly, still biologically active.

then.text: The fluid is warm and viscous, with a faint amber glow. It preserved you — and hundreds of other specimens — in suspended animation. The biochemistry is alien but clearly designed to sustain organic life.
You swirl the vial gently. The fluid moves like honey, clinging to the glass. Something about it feels... alive.

items.name: Pod Glass Shard
items.description: A curved shard from your broken stasis pod. Sharp enough to cut.

then.text: Translucent and curved, still faintly stained with amber fluid. The edges are razor-sharp. Not glass exactly — some alien composite that's stronger and lighter.
You test the edge against your thumb. It draws blood immediately. Careful with this.

items.name: Surgical Probe
items.description: An alien surgical instrument — curved bone-like material with a fine tip.

then.text: It looks grown rather than manufactured — smooth bone-like material tapering to a needle-fine point. The handle has organic ridges shaped for fingers much longer than yours. But it fits well enough in your small hands.

items.name: Containment Key Card
items.description: A bio-organic access card pulled from the security hub. Pulses faintly with stored energy.

then.text: Not plastic — something closer to compressed cartilage, embedded with bioluminescent circuits. It pulses like a heartbeat. Keyed to the containment deck's security systems.

items.name: Data Crystal — Personal Log
items.description: A small crystalline data storage device from the specimen archive. Contains a Choir officer's personal records.

then.text: The crystal is the size of your thumb, faceted, with internal light patterns that shift when you tilt it. A Choir personal log — and embedded in the data structure, fragments of a translation cipher. This is piece one of four.

items.name: Nutrient Paste Tube
items.description: A tube of grey nutrient slurry from the feeding station. Smells like wet cardboard and ozone.

then.text: Standard specimen feed. The tube is soft, organic material. The paste inside is grey, odorless, nutritionally complete for a dozen different species. Edible but unappetizing. Could also be used as bait — the drones are programmed to retrieve spilled feed.

items.name: Specimen Tag
items.description: Your own specimen identification tag from the stasis pod. Proof of what you are to them.

then.text: A small organic tag, pulled from your pod's label slot. Alien script — you can't read it yet — but it's your entry in their collection. Proof that you were catalogued. Proof that you exist as something more than a specimen.

items.name: Emergency Suit Helmet
items.description: An alien emergency space helmet. Too large for you, but still functional.

then.text: Designed for a Choir skull — far too large for you, but the visor seals automatically when worn. The internal atmosphere system still works. It would protect you from vacuum or toxic environments, even if it sits like a fishbowl on your shoulders.

items.name: Ventilation Map
items.description: Scratches in the vent shaft walls that form a crude map. You traced them onto a flat surface.

then.text: Someone — or something — scratched a map of the ventilation system into the shaft walls. Previous escape attempts. The map shows branching paths between containment sections, and marks dead ends with deep gouges. One path leads to the operational decks.

items.name: Severed Neural Tendril
items.description: A section of neural interface tendril, severed from a Choir dormancy alcove.

then.text: Rubbery, organic, about a foot long. The cut end still sparks faintly with bio-electric impulses. The Choir use these to interface with their ship's systems. With the right adapter, you could too — if you could trick it into accepting non-Choir biology.

items.name: Ship's Black Box
items.description: The Choir vessel's flight recorder. Contains the complete mission log — including records of every world consumed.

then.text: A dense, heavily shielded data device. It contains everything: navigation logs, mission parameters, specimen records, and communications with The Convergence. This is proof of what they've done — and what they're doing to the planet below.

items.name: Power Cell
items.description: A Choir power cell from engineering. Compact, immensely powerful, warm to the touch.

then.text: Bio-organic casing around a dense energy core. It hums faintly and radiates warmth. A single cell powers a Choir shuttle for weeks. Handle with care — damage to the casing would release the stored energy violently.

items.name: Resonance Disruptor
items.description: A Choir tool repurposed as a weapon. Emits a subsonic pulse that disrupts bio-mechanical systems.

then.text: Not a weapon by design — it's a maintenance tool for recalibrating Choir mechanisms. But aimed at a bio-organic lock, it scrambles the resonance patterns. Aimed at a drone, it disrupts motor functions for a few seconds. In your hands, it's the closest thing to a universal key.

items.name: Navigation Chip
items.description: A crystalline navigation module from the bridge. Contains star charts and jump coordinates.

then.text: A slim crystal wafer etched with navigation data. Star charts, jump coordinates, the Convergence's mapped path across galaxies. Without this, no ship leaves this system — the jump points are too complex to calculate manually.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 2
items.description: A data pattern extracted from the Choir's resonance chamber. The second piece of the translation key.

then.text: Extracted from the communal resonance patterns in the Choir's living quarters. Their 'language' is subsonic vibration, and this fragment maps vibration patterns to meaning. Combined with the other fragments, it could let you read all alien text.

items.name: Choir Resonance Crystal
items.description: A crystal from the ship's data core that resonates at the Choir's communication frequency.

then.text: Deep purple, perfectly smooth, vibrating at a frequency you can feel in your teeth. It's tuned to the Choir's subsonic communication band — a piece of their network made solid. The same resonance frequency the Convergence uses to control its harvesters.

items.name: Bio-Garden Extract
items.description: A concentrated extract from the ship's hydroponics bay. Bioluminescent, biochemically complex.

then.text: Harvested from the alien plants in the bio-garden. The extract glows faintly blue-green and contains an extraordinary density of biological compounds. The Choir uses it for everything from nutrition to neural repair. In the right combination, it could interface organic with crystalline systems.

items.name: Comm Array Schematics
items.description: Technical diagrams of the ship's communication array. Details frequencies, power requirements, and range.

then.text: Detailed schematics showing the communications array's architecture. Frequency ranges, power routing, targeting systems. With these, the array on the planet's nexus could be recalibrated to broadcast across the galaxy — if you could reach it.

items.name: Shuttle Fuel Line
items.description: A replacement fuel conduit for the damaged shuttle. Organic tubing with self-sealing connectors.

then.text: Bio-organic tubing that carries fuel from the bay's supply to the shuttle's engines. The connectors seal automatically when pressed into place. You'll need this, plus a power cell, to get the damaged shuttle flight-ready.

items.name: Drone Antenna
items.description: A sensory antenna pulled from a disabled maintenance drone. Still picks up Choir signals.

then.text: A thin, segmented antenna that twitches faintly in your hand — it's still receiving signals. It picks up the subsonic frequencies the Choir use to coordinate. Holding it near your ear, you can hear distant clicks and hums. An early warning system.

items.name: Coolant Flask
items.description: A sealed flask of reactor coolant from engineering. Extremely cold, mildly corrosive.

then.text: The flask is frosted on the outside — the coolant inside is near absolute zero. A crack in the seal would release a burst of freezing vapor. Useful for cooling overheated systems, or as an emergency weapon against anything organic.

items.name: Bio-Garden Fiber
items.description: Strong, flexible fiber harvested from alien plants. Tougher than any natural rope.

then.text: Harvested from the tendrils of the hydroponics plants. Incredibly strong and flexible — the Choir use it in construction and repair. It can be woven, tied, or wrapped. Combined with something sharp, it would make an excellent handle or binding.

items.name: Shuttle Emergency Beacon
items.description: A distress beacon from the crashed shuttle. Can recall any shuttle within signal range.

then.text: A compact transmitter designed to recall a shuttle to its beacon location. The signal range covers the entire planet. If there's a working shuttle in orbit or on the surface, this will bring it to you. Your ticket off this rock — if you choose to leave.

items.name: Wasteland Mineral Sample
items.description: Crystalline mineral from the base of a siphon tower. Infused with residual Convergence energy.

then.text: The soil near the siphon towers has been transformed — crystallized by the Convergence's energy extraction. This sample still holds a faint charge, a dampened echo of the energy that flows through the towers. It resists energy flow rather than conducting it.

items.name: Siphon Crystal Fragment
items.description: A fragment broken from an energy siphon tower. Pulses with raw Convergence energy.

then.text: It burns cold in your hand and crackles with contained energy. A piece of the Convergence's harvesting infrastructure, still charged with stolen planetary life force. Incredibly dangerous. Incredibly powerful. A key component for anything that needs to interact with Convergence energy systems.

items.name: Refugee Journal
items.description: A personal journal from the refugee camp. Written by a four-armed scientist in the final days.

then.text: The journal of Dr. Kaelith, a physicist who fled the city when the siphons began. Entries detail the final days — the panic, the failed defenses, the evacuation that came too late. Embedded in the margins: notation patterns that match the translation cipher format. Fragment three of four.

items.name: Fungal Extract
items.description: A concentrated extract from the bioluminescent fungi in the grove. Glows purple in the dark.

then.text: The fungi survived the Convergence's harvesting — they feed on the residual energy rather than being drained by it. The extract has remarkable properties: it promotes healing in organic tissue and, combined with the right compounds, can suppress neural detection.

items.name: Echo Stabilizer
items.description: Military-grade alien technology from the bunker. Stabilizes the energy field around Echoes, making them safe to approach.

then.text: A handheld device that projects a stabilization field. The planet's military developed it to study the Echoes — remnants of their people trapped in the Convergence's energy. It calms the chaotic energy patterns, making Echoes coherent enough to interact with safely. Without it, getting close to an Echo is like standing in a lightning storm.

items.name: Alien Sidearm
items.description: A four-armed species' personal weapon. Energy-based, partially charged.

then.text: Designed for a four-armed grip — you need both hands to hold it steady. The energy cell is partially depleted: maybe six shots. Each shot is devastatingly loud. Use it wisely, or not at all.

items.name: Bunker Defense Schematics
items.description: Military blueprints showing the planet's defense strategy against the Convergence.

then.text: Detailed military plans for the planet's last stand. Orbital defense satellite positions, ground-based weapon emplacements, and — most importantly — partial schematics for a weapon designed to disrupt the Convergence's energy systems. The plans are incomplete, but they confirm the weapon was built.

items.name: Survival Rations
items.description: Preserved alien food from the refugee camp. Still sealed, still edible.

then.text: Vacuum-sealed packages of concentrated nutrition. The labels show a four-armed figure eating contentedly. Not designed for your biology, but close enough. Eating one restores energy and clears your head.

items.name: Signal Flare
items.description: An emergency signal flare from the crashed shuttle. Burns bright, burns loud.

then.text: A human-made signal flare from the Outrider's emergency kit. Pull the cap and it burns blinding white for thirty seconds. Useful as a signal, a light source, a distraction, or — wrapped with the right material — an improvised torch.

items.name: Climbing Pitons
items.description: Metal spikes from the refugee camp's supplies. Designed for climbing rocky terrain.

then.text: Alien-made climbing aids — hardened metal spikes with looped heads for roping. The refugees used them to navigate the wasteland's shattered terrain. Essential for vertical surfaces your small stature can't otherwise reach.

items.name: Radiation Badge
items.description: A sensor badge from the bunker. Changes color in the presence of dangerous Convergence energy.

then.text: A simple but effective device — the crystalline strip changes color from green (safe) to yellow (caution) to red (lethal). The planet's military used them to navigate near siphon towers and Convergence infrastructure. Near the nexus, it'll be essential for finding safe paths.

items.name: City Keystone
items.description: An ornamental keystone from the grand plaza's central statue. Opens restricted areas throughout the city.

then.text: A crystalline key shaped like a miniature four-armed figure. It was built into the plaza's central statue — a city administrator's master key. It interfaces with the city's door systems, granting access to government buildings, the war room, and restricted infrastructure.

items.name: Translation Cipher Fragment 4
items.description: The final fragment of the translation cipher, found in the city's library.

then.text: The library's master index contained the final cipher fragment — a Rosetta stone the city's linguists compiled to communicate with the Choir during failed negotiations. With all four fragments, you can read every piece of alien text in the game.

items.name: Weapon Core
items.description: The heart of the civilization's countermeasure weapon. A dense crystalline sphere pulsing with contained energy.

then.text: Heavy for its size — it feels like holding a small star. The weapon core was designed to resonate at the Convergence's own frequency, turning its stolen energy back on itself. Alone it's inert. Combined with the right components, it becomes the key to destroying the nexus.

items.name: Defense Grid Controller
items.description: A command module for the planet's orbital defense satellite network.

then.text: The planet's last line of defense — a controller for orbital weapons satellites. Most satellites are destroyed, but a few remain dormant in orbit. With enough power, they could be reactivated for one devastating strike.

items.name: Alien Personal Locket
items.description: A delicate locket from a residential home. Contains a holographic family portrait.

then.text: A small crystalline locket on a chain. Inside: a holographic portrait of a four-armed family — two adults, three children, all smiling. The youngest is holding a toy that looks like a simplified version of the siphon towers. They had no idea what was coming. Carrying this near coherent Echoes triggers powerful reactions.

items.name: Power Cell Adapter
items.description: An adapter that bridges the planet's technology with alien power sources.

then.text: The city's engineers designed this to interface their technology with captured Choir power cells. It converts between bio-organic energy formats and the civilization's crystalline power systems. A universal translator for alien technology.

items.name: Prophet's Crystal
items.description: A sacred crystal from the temple. Shows visions of possible futures when held.

then.text: The temple's priests used crystals like this for divination — and they were right more often than chance allows. Holding it, you see flashes: a nexus in flames. A signal reaching distant stars. A crystalline intelligence, afraid. A small creature, choosing. The visions are fragmented but feel profoundly real.

items.name: Railway Pass Token
items.description: An access token for the city's underground transit system.

then.text: A small crystalline disc — a transit pass. The underground railway still has power in some sections. This token activates the rail cars, allowing fast travel between the city's districts. The tunnels also connect to deeper passages beneath the city.

items.name: Resonance Tuning Fork
items.description: A ceremonial tuning fork from the temple. Vibrates at the frequency of the former civilization's communication.

then.text: The four-armed species communed through vibration, like the Choir but natural. This tuning fork produces their base resonance frequency. Combined with the Echo Stabilizer, it could enable full two-way communication with coherent Echoes — letting you truly speak with the dead.

items.name: Lab Safety Goggles
items.description: Protective eyewear from the research lab. Filters dangerous energy wavelengths.

then.text: Oversized for your face but functional. The lenses filter the blinding energy wavelengths produced by Convergence systems. The researchers wore these when studying siphon tower samples. Essential for looking directly at high-energy areas without going blind.

items.name: Ancient Blueprint
items.description: Complete assembly instructions for the countermeasure weapon. Found in the research lab.

then.text: A holographic blueprint showing the complete countermeasure weapon assembly. Three components: a primed weapon core, an energy dampener, and a siphon crystal fragment. The assembly order is critical — wrong sequence damages the core. Core first, dampener second, crystal last.

items.name: Convergence Energy Sample
items.description: Pure Convergence energy contained in a crystalline vial. Incredibly dangerous.

then.text: The vial is cold enough to burn and bright enough to read by. Inside: pure harvested planetary energy — the lifeforce of an entire world, concentrated. The crystal containment barely holds it. This is what the Convergence feeds on. This is what it's stealing.

items.name: Ancient Access Key
items.description: A key from the Convergence's stasis gallery. Opens the deepest sections of the nexus.

then.text: Not Choir-made. Not from the planet's civilization. This key predates both — it belongs to the Convergence itself, or whatever built the original nexus infrastructure. A crystalline fractal pattern that interfaces with the oldest locks in the structure.

items.name: Curator's Signal Device
items.description: The Curator's personal communication device. Can call the Choir vessel from orbit.

then.text: Taken from — or given by — the Curator itself. This device is keyed to the Curator's authority aboard the Choir vessel. It can recall the ship, issue commands to drones, and override security protocols. In friendly hands, it's a powerful ally. In desperate hands, it's a weapon.

items.name: Core Interface Module
items.description: A module from the control spire that allows direct neural interface with the Convergence intelligence.

then.text: The Choir use these to receive instructions from the Convergence. It translates crystalline energy patterns into neural signals and vice versa. It wasn't designed for non-Choir biology, but with the right biochemical preparation, it could bridge any mind to the Convergence. The question is whether you'd come back.

items.name: Escape Shaft Key
items.description: A mechanical key that opens the former civilization's emergency escape shaft in the nexus.

then.text: Found in the weapon assembly area — the former civilization's staging ground for their assault on the nexus. This key opens the emergency shaft they carved as an exit route. The shaft leads up and out, to the planet's surface. Your way out, if you choose to take it.

items.name: Charged Sidearm
items.description: A charged sidearm.

then.text: You examine the charged sidearm.

items.name: Complete Translation Cipher
items.description: A complete translation cipher.

then.text: You examine the complete translation cipher.

items.name: Countermeasure Stage2
items.description: A countermeasure stage2.

then.text: You examine the countermeasure stage2.

items.name: Echo Communicator
items.description: A echo communicator.

then.text: You examine the echo communicator.

items.name: Energy Dampener
items.description: A energy dampener.

then.text: You examine the energy dampener.

items.name: Improvised Torch
items.description: A improvised torch.

then.text: You examine the improvised torch.

items.description: A neural suppressant.

then.text: You examine the neural suppressant.

items.description: A orbital weapon.

then.text: You examine the orbital weapon.

items.description: A overcharge device.

then.text: You examine the overcharge device.

items.description: A partial cipher 12.

then.text: You examine the partial cipher 12.

items.description: A partial cipher 123.

then.text: You examine the partial cipher 123.

items.name: Primed Weapon Core
items.description: A primed weapon core.

then.text: You examine the primed weapon core.

items.name: Reinforced Blade
items.description: A reinforced blade.

then.text: You examine the reinforced blade.

items.name: Sedative Compound
items.description: A sedative compound.

then.text: You examine the sedative compound.

items.name: Shielded Helmet
items.description: A shielded helmet.

then.text: You examine the shielded helmet.

items.description: A the countermeasure.

then.text: You examine the the countermeasure.

items.name: Universal Bypass
items.description: A universal bypass.

then.text: You examine the universal bypass.

items.name: Universal Interface
items.description: A universal interface.

then.text: You examine the universal interface.

items.name: Galactic Broadcast
items.description: A pre-recorded galactic broadcast signal, ready for transmission.

then.text: A carefully prepared broadcast signal containing evidence of the harvest conspiracy. If transmitted, it could alert the galactic community.

items.name: Neural Bridge
items.description: A device that creates a direct neural link between minds.

then.text: An alien neural bridge device. It could establish a direct mental connection with the Nexus consciousness.

combinations.message: You wrap the bio-fiber tightly around the base of the glass shard, creating a secure grip. The alien fiber bonds to the glass — stronger than tape, flexible as leather. A proper blade now.

You mix the nutrient paste with the stasis fluid. The combination reacts — the paste absorbs the fluid and turns a deep amber. The stasis biochemistry that kept you unconscious for days is now concentrated in a smearable compound. Touch it and sleep.

You pulse the disruptor through the key card's bio-circuits, overwriting its access restrictions. The card flares bright, then settles to a steady glow. It no longer identifies as a specific access level — it identifies as ALL access levels.

The mineral dissolves into the stasis fluid, and the mixture crystallizes into a dense gel that absorbs energy on contact. A palm-sized blob that drinks power. Near Convergence systems, it creates a local dead zone.

You channel the disruptor's pulse through the siphon crystal. The crystal amplifies it a hundredfold — the device now emits a burst capable of overloading any energy system it's aimed at. One shot. Make it count.

The fungal extract reacts with the sedative compound, producing a paste that suppresses neural signatures. Smeared on your skin, it makes you invisible to anything that detects by energy pattern — including Echoes.

You align the two cipher fragments. The data patterns interlock — half the translation key is now complete. You can read simple alien text, but complex inscriptions still elude you. Two more fragments to go.
The refugee journal's margin notations complete a third of the cipher. The translation is becoming clearer — you can now read most operational text. One fragment remains.

The final fragment locks into place. The complete cipher unfolds in your mind like a language you always knew but forgot. Every alien inscription, every label, every record — readable. The universe just opened up.

You press the Choir crystal against the weapon core. The resonance frequency syncs — the core begins to hum, vibrating at the Convergence's own frequency. It's alive now, tuned to destroy the thing it was made to fight. Partially assembled. It needs a dampener and a power source.

The adapter accepts the navigation chip's crystalline format and bridges it to a universal power bus. The result is a device that can interface with any alien technology — Choir, Convergence, or the former civilization's systems. A skeleton key for machines.

You wire the overcharge device into the defense grid controller. The orbital satellites now have a targeting solution — and enough power for one devastating strike. Point it at the nexus and fire. Point it at the Choir ship and fire. Either way, everything changes.

You wrap the bio-fiber around the flare's head, creating a longer-burning light source. The alien fiber catches fire slowly and burns steady instead of blinding. A proper torch that'll last much longer than the flare alone.

You line the helmet's interior with the energy dampener gel. The dampener absorbs the worst of the Convergence's ambient radiation. Wearing this, you can survive the nexus's high-energy chambers without your nervous system frying.

You mount the tuning fork in the stabilizer's emitter array. The combined device doesn't just calm Echoes — it speaks their language. The stabilization field now carries your words as resonance patterns the dead can hear. And their responses come back clear.

The Choir power cell slots into the alien weapon's depleted energy chamber. The sidearm hums to life — fully charged now. Twenty shots instead of six. The four-armed grip is awkward, but the firepower is undeniable.

The energy dampener wraps around the primed core, containing its resonance while focusing its destructive potential. One more component — the siphon crystal fragment — and the countermeasure is complete.

The siphon crystal fragment snaps into the dampener housing like it was always meant to be there. The complete countermeasure weapon activates — a sphere of crystallized destruction, humming with the Convergence's own stolen energy turned against it. This kills planets. This saves them too.

objects.name: Your Broken Pod
objects.description: The stasis pod you woke in. The glass is cracked, amber fluid pooling beneath it. Fragments of the pod casing litter the floor.

then.text: Your stasis pod. The glass is fractured in a web of cracks, amber fluid seeping from the widest one. You're still half-inside it. The malfunction that freed you left shrapnel and fluid everywhere. Something glints in the drainage channel — a shard of pod glass, sharp as a knife.
The pod hangs open, drained of fluid. Your outline is still visible in the residue on the back wall — a small creature's impression in amber. A specimen tag dangles from the pod's frame.

You brace your feet against the pod's inner wall and push. The cracked glass groans, splinters, and finally gives way with a wet crunch. Amber fluid gushes out around you as you tumble free onto the cold floor. You're out. You're loose.
You carefully snap off a curved shard of pod glass from the broken edge. It's razor-sharp — some alien composite that's stronger and lighter than real glass. A crude tool, but a tool nonetheless.

objects.name: Drainage Channel
objects.description: A channel beneath the pods where spilled stasis fluid collects before being recycled.

then.text: A shallow channel cut into the floor, feeding into the ship's recycling systems. Amber stasis fluid pools here, slowly draining. The fluid shimmers with faint bioluminescence.

You cup your hands and scoop up some of the amber fluid. It's warm and viscous, almost alive. You need a container... wait — one of the sample jars from the processing lab would work. Actually, a small amount clings to a curved pod fragment, enough to seal in the shard itself. You carefully collect a vial's worth.

objects.name: Occupied Stasis Pods
objects.description: Rows of intact pods stretching into the shadows above. Most contain dead specimens. Some glow faintly — still active.

then.text: You peer closely at the wall of amber pods. Each one contains a different specimen, suspended in stasis fluid. Alien script labels identify each creature.

interactions.response: You tap on the nearest pod's surface. The amber fluid inside swirls briefly. The creature within doesn't stir.

objects.name: Specimen Tag
objects.description: A small tag hanging from your pod's frame, inscribed with alien notation.

then.text: A small bio-organic tag, like a leaf made of cartilage. Alien notation is etched into its surface — your classification, probably. A serial number for a specimen. It identifies you as a collected organism. It's proof you were here. Proof you existed to them.
You snap the tag free from the pod frame. It's small enough to pocket. You're not a specimen. You're a person. But this might be useful as proof — to someone, somewhere — that you were here.

objects.name: Pod Labels
objects.description: Alien script labels on each pod in the cluster, with numerical sequences.

then.text: Alien script you can't read, but there are numerical sequences that might be universal — each pod has a six-digit code. The codes follow a pattern: each shares the same first four digits, with the last two being the pod's position in the hexagonal arrangement. The first four digits might be a section code... like a room number. Or an access code.
The pod labels are clear now — the first four digits ARE the section access code. You've already noted it for the processing lab door.

You trace the numerical sequences across multiple pods, comparing patterns. The first four digits are identical: 7-3-1-9. That's not random — it's a section identifier. The processing lab door has a keypad. This could be the access code.

objects.name: Pod Cluster Controls
objects.description: Bio-organic control panels between the pods with fleshy buttons and tendon-like cables.

then.text: Bio-organic buttons that pulse softly — grown, not manufactured. Tendril-like cables connect each panel to the central processing node above. These controls manage the stasis pods: temperature, fluid levels, sedation. Everything to keep specimens alive and docile.

You press one of the fleshy buttons experimentally. A nearby pod flickers — the fluid inside cloudss momentarily. The specimen twitches. You decide not to press anything else without understanding the system better.

objects.name: Preserved Insect Specimen
objects.description: A large insect-like creature perfectly preserved in amber fluid inside one of the hexagonal pods.

then.text: A creature the size of a large dog — six legs, iridescent carapace, compound eyes that catch the bioluminescent light. It's perfectly preserved, curled in a resting position. Its world is probably dead now, consumed like all the others marked in red on the archive's holographic display. This is all that remains of its kind.

objects.name: Examination Tables
objects.description: Long tables with organic restraints, designed for specimens much larger than you.

then.text: Two examination tables dominate the room. The restraints are sized for creatures far larger than you — thick organic clamps that would hold a Choir member. Drainage channels lead to floor grates. Residue stains tell stories you don't want to hear. These tables have seen a lot of use.

You climb onto the nearest table. Standing on it gives you a better view of the room — and access to the higher shelves. The restraints twitch when you touch them, sensing biomass. You step back quickly.

objects.name: Surgical Instrument Rack
objects.description: A rack of alien surgical tools — curved bone-like instruments, probes, and extractors.

then.text: Surgical instruments arranged with obsessive precision. They look grown rather than forged — smooth bone-like material, organic curves, needle-fine tips. Most are sized for Choir hands: too large for you to wield. But a smaller probe near the bottom of the rack looks manageable.

You reach for the smallest instrument — a probe with a fine, flexible tip. It fits well enough in your hands. The bone-like material is warm to the touch, almost alive. It'll work as a precision tool — lock picks, screws, delicate mechanisms.

objects.name: Sample Jars
objects.description: Shelves of preserved biological samples in sealed jars.

then.text: Dozens of sealed jars containing biological samples — tissue, fluid, organs. Each is labeled with the same alien notation you've seen on the pods. Some samples are recognizable (a heart, an eye), others are abstract shapes in fluid. Your stomach turns.

objects.name: Lab Data Screens
objects.description: Screens cycling through biological data and procedural information.

then.text: The screens cycle through processing routines: intake, classification, preservation, disposal. One screen shows what appears to be a startup sequence — a series of bio-organic buttons being pressed in a specific order. It's demonstrating the security console procedure for someone (or something) learning the system.

You study the startup sequence carefully, memorizing the pattern of button presses. Five steps, specific order, specific timing. This is the security hub's console sequence — you're sure of it. The Choir trains its drones using these demonstration loops.

objects.name: Specimen Drawers
objects.description: Walls of drawers containing failed specimens. Most are sealed. One is partially open.

then.text: Rows of drawers, floor to ceiling, each large enough to hold a body. Most are sealed. The one that's open contains something wrapped in organic membrane — humanoid in shape, roughly your size. Whatever it was, it didn't survive the collection process.

You slide the open drawer further out. The creature inside is... similar to you. Same general build, same proportions. A different species, but close enough to be unsettling. It didn't make it. You almost didn't either.

objects.name: Autopsy Slab
objects.description: A central examination surface with drainage channels and overhead lighting.

then.text: A slab designed for dissection. Drainage channels lead to the recycling vats. Overhead, articulated lighting rigs are frozen mid-position, aimed at where a specimen's torso would be. The slab is clean — recently used and cleaned. The Choir is thorough.

objects.name: Recycling Vats
objects.description: Large vats where failed specimens are dissolved and their biological material reclaimed.

then.text: Three vats of viscous green liquid, bubbling slowly. The ship recycles everything — failed specimens become raw material for the bio-gardens, the hull, the instruments. Nothing is wasted. Nothing leaves.

objects.name: Severed Neural Tendril
objects.description: A neural connection tendril, severed during the struggle that damaged the security hub.

then.text: A length of neural tendril, the kind the Choir use to interface with the ship's systems. This one is severed — torn during whatever struggle damaged the security hub. The cut end still pulses faintly with residual bio-electricity. It's gross. It might also be useful.

You pick up the tendril, suppressing a shudder. It's warm and slightly damp, like holding a severed worm. The bio-electricity makes your fingers tingle. Choir technology interfaces through these — plug this into the right port and you might be able to access systems keyed to their biology.

objects.name: Nutrient Dispenser
objects.description: An automated dispenser that drips grey nutrient paste into troughs at regular intervals.

then.text: A mechanical arm dispenses grey slurry into feeding troughs on a timer. The paste smells like metal and algae. It's sustenance — barely. The dispenser connects to a central nutrient tank via transparent tubes.
You collect a tube's worth of nutrient paste from the dispenser output. It's disgusting, but the Choir drones are attracted to it — it could serve as a distraction if you need one.

objects.name: Feeding Troughs
objects.description: Long troughs filled with grey nutrient paste for living specimens.

then.text: Shallow troughs of grey nutrient paste, half-eaten. The paste is replenished automatically. Something has been feeding here recently — you can see marks in the paste where a creature has scooped it out.

objects.name: Specimen Enclosures
objects.description: Small enclosures behind shimmering energy barriers, holding living specimens.

then.text: Behind flickering energy barriers, living specimens pace in small enclosures. One enclosure holds something canine-like with too many legs. Another contains a creature that's mostly tentacles. They're alive, aware, and miserable. They watch you with recognition — another prisoner.

You try making sounds at the nearest creature. It stops pacing and stares at you through the barrier. It makes a low, mournful sound in return. You don't share a language, but you share a situation. It returns to pacing.

objects.name: Scratch Marks
objects.description: Deep scratches gouged into the ventilation shaft walls — previous escape attempts.

then.text: Deep gouges in the organic walls, made by claws or tools. Someone else navigated these vents before you. The scratches form patterns — not random panic, but deliberate markings. Arrows, symbols, a crude map of the shaft system etched by a predecessor who wanted the next escapee to find their way.

You trace the scratch-map with your fingers, memorizing the layout. Three main routes: one leads back to the stasis hold, one to the feeding station, one to what's marked with a crude eye symbol — the security hub. Whoever made this got further than the Choir expected.

objects.name: Shaft Branches
objects.description: The ventilation shaft splits into multiple directions, each marked by dim red maintenance lights.

then.text: The shaft branches in three directions, each vanishing into darkness beyond the dim red maintenance lights. Without a guide, choosing wrong could leave you lost in the ship's circulation system for hours — or worse, drop you into machinery.

With the scratch-map to guide you, the branches make sense. Left leads back to the stasis hold. Center leads to the feeding station. Right — marked with the eye symbol — leads to the security hub. The ship's ventilation connects everything on this deck.

objects.name: Security Console
objects.description: The main control station for containment deck security. Multiple screens show surveillance feeds.

then.text: The main security console — bio-organic buttons arranged in a semicircle around a central display. Surveillance feeds from across the containment deck flicker on damaged screens. One screen clearly shows a tall, methodical figure moving through corridors. The Curator, making its rounds. The console is in standby mode, awaiting an activation sequence.

You press buttons experimentally. The console flashes red — incorrect sequence. An alarm chirps once before going silent. You freeze. Nothing happens... but you've added noise. You need to find the correct startup sequence.

You enter the startup sequence from the lab's demonstration display. Five buttons, specific order, specific timing. The console hums to life. Screens sharpen. A ship layout map materializes on the central display — the entire vessel, deck by deck. And there — a containment lock override. You could unlock every door on this deck.
You trigger the containment lock override. Every sealed door on the containment deck clicks open simultaneously. The Curator will notice — but now you have access to everything.

objects.name: Cracked Surveillance Screen
objects.description: One of the surveillance screens is badly cracked — someone or something fought here.

then.text: The screen is cracked in a starburst pattern — something impacted it hard. The surrounding console has scorch marks. A chair is knocked over nearby. Someone fought the Choir here. The Choir won, obviously. But whoever it was put up a fight.

objects.name: Security Drawer
objects.description: A drawer beneath the security console, partially jammed open.

then.text: A drawer jammed partially open — probably from the fight. Inside, you can see bio-organic key cards, each a different shade. These are access cards for the containment deck's various sections.
You pull out a key card — it pulses like a heartbeat in your palm. Bio-organic circuitry embedded in compressed cartilage. This should open any standard containment door on the ship.

objects.name: Data Crystal Archive
objects.description: Floor-to-ceiling racks of glowing data crystals — each one a species' complete biological record.

then.text: Thousands of data crystals, each humming at a slightly different frequency. The collection spans millennia — some crystals are ancient, their glow faded. Others are bright and new. Each one represents an entire species, catalogued and filed. A library of extinction.

You pull a crystal at random and slot it into the reading device. An alien species fills the holographic display — six-legged, fur-covered, intelligent eyes. Below it: a world, lush and green. And the red symbol. Consumed. You replace the crystal, feeling sick.

objects.name: Misplaced Data Crystal
objects.description: A crystal that's slightly different from the others — personal records rather than specimen data.

then.text: This crystal is different — smaller, a different hue. It's been misfiled among the specimen records. When you hold it up to the light, it pulses with a more complex pattern. Personal data, not biological. A Choir officer's private log, perhaps.

You pocket the crystal. It contains notation you can't read yet — alien script mixed with mathematical sequences. But there are patterns here that look like a translation key. Fragment one of something larger. If you can find more fragments, you might be able to read what the Choir writes.

objects.name: Crystal Reading Device
objects.description: A pedestal-mounted device for reading data crystals, projecting holographic content.

then.text: A crystalline reading device on an ornate pedestal. Slot a data crystal in and it projects the contents as a hologram above. The interface seems universal — it displays whatever species' biology is recorded on the crystal. Efficient, clinical, deeply impersonal.

You slot the personal log crystal into the reader. A flood of alien text fills the air — dense, layered, incomprehensible. But between the text: diagrams, star maps, what look like personal sketches. This Choir officer was methodical, recording everything. And buried in the notation — translation keys. Partial ones. You'd need more fragments to complete the cipher, but this is a start.

objects.name: Holographic Planet Display
objects.description: Holographic projections of cataloged worlds drifting slowly above the archive, most marked in red.

then.text: Dozens of planets drift overhead in miniature hologram — lush worlds, ice worlds, gas giants with inhabited moons. Almost all are marked with the red consumption symbol. The scale is staggering. The Convergence hasn't consumed dozens of worlds. It has consumed hundreds. Thousands. Across galaxies, across epochs. This archive stretches back billions of years.

objects.name: Viewport
objects.description: A large viewport showing the planet below — beautiful from orbit, unaware it's dying.

then.text: The planet fills the viewport. Blue oceans, green continents, wisps of white cloud. From up here it looks healthy, alive, beautiful. But you can see them now — thin beams of light descending from orbit to the surface. Energy siphons. The Convergence is already feeding. The planet doesn't know it's dying.

objects.name: Empty Docking Clamps
objects.description: Heavy mechanical clamps where your ship, the Outrider, was once docked. The clamps are open and empty.

then.text: The docking clamps are open, still showing the outline of your ship's hull in wear patterns. The Outrider — your ship, your home, your way out — was jettisoned. Probably automated: the Choir don't want escape vehicles lying around for specimens to find. Your ship is gone. You're not leaving this way.

objects.name: Emergency Suit Locker
objects.description: A locker containing alien emergency space suits, designed for Choir physiology.

then.text: Emergency suit locker — standard safety equipment near an airlock. The suits inside are sized for the Choir: far too large for you. But the helmets...

You pull the locker open. Three Choir emergency suits hang inside — massive, organic-looking, completely unwearable for someone your size. But the helmets are modular, designed to seal independently. One might fit you, barely, worn like an oversized bucket on your head.
You pull the smallest helmet free. It's still too big, but the internal padding can be adjusted. It'll protect against vacuum, toxins, and energy bursts — at least briefly. Better than nothing.

objects.name: Manual Override Panel
objects.description: A heavily locked manual override panel for the airlock blast doors.

then.text: A manual override panel for the airlock doors, covered by heavy bio-organic locks. Even if you opened it, the blast doors lead to vacuum — and your ship isn't on the other side anymore. But the override circuitry might be useful for other purposes.
The locks are bio-organic and heavy — designed to prevent accidental decompression. You can't force them open with your bare hands.

The containment key card interfaces with the lock. The panel opens, revealing override controls. You won't be using the airlock itself — but you've learned how the ship's override systems work. This knowledge will help with other locked systems.

objects.name: Sealed Blast Doors
objects.description: Heavy organic-metallic blast doors sealing the airlock from the corridor.

then.text: Massive blast doors designed to contain decompression. These lead to the outer airlock — and beyond that, vacuum. They're sealed for a reason. Even if you could open them, there's nothing on the other side but death.

objects.name: Holographic Star Map
objects.description: A massive hologram showing the Convergence's path across galaxies — hundreds of consumed systems marked in red.

then.text: Hundreds of star systems traced in light, spanning multiple galaxies. The consumed ones glow red — there are so many they form a trail, a path of destruction stretching back across cosmic time. The current system pulses amber: in progress. Not yet consumed. Not yet dead.

You manipulate the star map controls, zooming into the local cluster. Your home system is visible — unmarked, untouched, ignorant. The path of consumption hasn't reached it yet. But the trajectory is clear. It will. You memorize key coordinates and navigation data.

objects.name: Command Console
objects.description: The primary command station, grown into the floor like a mushroom. Navigation controls and the ship's flight systems.

then.text: The command console is a bio-organic workstation grown from the floor, its surface covered in responsive membranes and neural interfaces. A navigation chip slot is visible — the ship's course is set by physical media, not software. Remove the chip, change the course.

You reach into the navigation slot and extract a small crystalline chip — the ship's current course data, including coordinates for the nearest relay stations and jump points. With this chip and a working shuttle, you could navigate out of this system.

objects.name: Command Throne
objects.description: A seat designed for the ship's commander, with neural interface tendrils hanging from a headrest.

then.text: The command throne is massive — built for a Choir commander twice your height. Neural interface tendrils hang from the headrest like limp tentacles, waiting to connect to a Choir's nervous system. Through that connection, the commander would feel the entire ship as an extension of their body.

You press the severed tendril against the throne's interface port. For a flash, you feel the ship — a vast, cold awareness. Corridors like veins. The reactor like a heart. The Curator's precise footsteps somewhere below. Then the connection breaks. The tendril doesn't have enough bio-electricity to maintain it. But you felt it — the ship is alive, and it knows you're aboard.

objects.name: Organic Reactor
objects.description: A massive pulsing organic reactor — like a beating heart wrapped in mechanical cables and transparent coolant tubes.

then.text: The reactor is a living thing — a heart the size of a house, wrapped in mechanical supports and coolant systems. With each pulse, the entire room shudders. Transparent tubes carry glowing coolant through a circulatory system. The vibration masks most sounds in here — good for hiding, terrible for hearing someone approach.

objects.name: Reactor Access Panel
objects.description: A maintenance panel on the reactor housing, where power cells are installed and removed.

then.text: A maintenance access panel on the reactor casing. Behind it, power cells are slotted into the reactor's distribution grid — portable energy sources that can be removed and used elsewhere. The panel is held shut by organic fasteners.

You pry the fasteners loose and swing the panel open. Inside: a grid of power cells, each glowing with stored reactor energy. Most are locked into the grid, but one on the edge can be disconnected without triggering a system alert.

You carefully disconnect the edge power cell. It comes free with a click and a brief flicker in the lighting — the reactor compensates almost instantly. The cell is warm, heavy, and full of energy. This could power a shuttle... or anything else that needs a boost.

objects.name: Coolant Distribution System
objects.description: Transparent tubes carrying glowing coolant through the engineering bay.

then.text: Glowing blue coolant flows through transparent tubes, keeping the reactor from overheating. The tubes branch and merge in patterns that look almost organic — because they are. The coolant itself is bio-active, a living fluid that absorbs and dissipates heat.

You find a maintenance flask near a junction point and fill it from a coolant bleed valve. The blue liquid is ice-cold despite the surrounding heat. Useful for cooling overheated systems — or as an emergency weapon. The stuff freezes on contact with warm surfaces.

objects.name: Power Distribution Panel
objects.description: A toggle panel controlling power distribution across the ship's operational systems.

then.text: A panel of bio-organic toggles controlling power distribution across the ship. Each toggle routes reactor energy to different systems: life support, weapons, navigation, shuttle bay, communications. Currently all systems are powered. Redirecting power could create opportunities — and risks.

You study the toggle layout. Routing extra power to the shuttle bay would speed launch prep, but the power has to come from somewhere. You could reduce weapons systems — the Choir would notice eventually, but it would buy time. You carefully reroute power to the shuttle bay systems.

objects.name: Communications Dish
objects.description: A dish-like apparatus suspended in the center of the room, surrounded by crystalline amplifiers.

then.text: The dish apparatus channels the Choir's subsonic communications across vast distances. Crystalline amplifiers boost the signal, turning thought-vibrations into interstellar transmissions. Through this array, the Choir reports to the Convergence. Every species catalogued, every planet consumed — logged and transmitted.

objects.name: Recording Station
objects.description: Where the Choir logs its reports to the Convergence. A strange microphone-like device and data storage.

then.text: A recording station where the Choir dictates mission reports. The 'microphone' is a resonance sensor that captures subsonic vibrations. Stored reports are kept on crystalline media — and one storage unit contains something different. A ship's black box recorder, standard deep-space salvage equipment. Your black box. From the Outrider.

You pull the Outrider's black box from the storage unit. It's human tech — your tech — scratched and battered but intact. It contains your ship's logs: your identity, your mission, your species' existence. Proof that you came here on purpose, not as livestock. Proof of sentience.

objects.name: Schematic Display
objects.description: Technical displays showing the communications array's internal architecture and transmission protocols.

then.text: Technical schematics for the communications array — transmission frequencies, amplifier configurations, targeting protocols. This is how the Choir talks to the stars. With these schematics, someone could build — or hijack — a transmission system.

You extract the schematic data onto a portable crystal. The comm array's blueprints — frequencies, power requirements, targeting algorithms. With this and enough power, you could broadcast on the Convergence's own network. Send a message to anyone listening.

objects.name: Frequency Dial
objects.description: A dial for tuning the comm array's transmission frequency. Currently locked to the Convergence's channel.

then.text: A frequency dial locked to the Convergence's communication channel. Tuning it to a different frequency could intercept other transmissions — or let you eavesdrop on the Convergence's own communications. The correct intercept frequency is probably in the bridge's navigation data.
The dial has hundreds of positions. Without knowing the correct frequency, you'd be tuning blind. The bridge's star charts might contain frequency data for Convergence communications channels.

Using the frequency data from the bridge's star charts, you tune the dial to the Convergence's primary command channel. Static resolves into subsonic patterns — you can't understand them, but the array's translation buffer renders a partial decode. Communications about the harvest's progress. Timetables. And coordinates for other harvesting operations across the galaxy.

objects.name: Weapons Rack
objects.description: Racks of Choir weapons — resonance staffs, energy projectors, containment nets. Most are biometrically locked.

then.text: Racks of Choir weapons — elegant, lethal, and completely useless to you. Each one is biometrically locked to its assigned handler's physiology. The resonance staffs hum when you approach. The energy projectors are too heavy to lift. But one device near the bottom looks different — smaller, more tool than weapon.

You pull the small device from the rack — a resonance disruptor. Not a weapon exactly, but a tool that disrupts bio-organic mechanisms. It vibrates in your hand, countering the frequencies that Choir tech uses. Locks, barriers, organic circuits — this thing scrambles them all.

objects.name: Weapon Maintenance Bench
objects.description: A workbench for maintaining and repairing Choir weapons.

then.text: Tools for maintaining bio-organic weaponry — tuning forks, growth accelerants, resonance calibrators. A damaged weapon sits half-disassembled, its innards exposed. The Choir maintains its arsenal with surgical precision.

objects.name: Empty Rack Slot
objects.description: A gap in the weapon rack where something was recently removed.

then.text: A gap in the rack where a weapon was removed recently — the mounting hooks are still warm. Whatever was here, the Curator took it. Recently. That means the Curator is armed with something beyond its natural manipulators. Be careful.

objects.name: Resonance Chamber
objects.description: A circular depression in the floor that glows with subsonic energy — the Choir's communal communication space.

then.text: The resonance chamber is how the Choir speaks — not with words but with vibrations. Standing at the edge, you feel patterns in the subsonic hum: data, emotions, shared memory. Among the patterns, something stands out — a translation matrix. The Choir learned this world's languages when they arrived. A fragment of that learning is encoded in the chamber's resonance.

You step into the chamber and let the vibrations wash over you. Among the subsonic noise, you isolate a pattern — a translation fragment, the Choir's Rosetta Stone for this region of space. Combined with other fragments, it could decode alien text across multiple species. Fragment two of the translation cipher.

objects.name: Dormant Choir Members
objects.description: Choir members standing motionless in wall alcoves, connected to the ship by neural tendrils from their backs.

then.text: Tall, eyeless figures standing upright in alcoves, neural tendrils connecting their spines to the ship's walls. They're dormant — not sleeping exactly, but in a low-power state, their consciousness merged with the ship's systems. They dream in data. One twitches occasionally, its manipulator limbs flexing in some automated reflex.

You reach toward the nearest dormant Choir member and immediately think better of it. Its skin is warm, faintly vibrating. The neural tendrils pulse with data. Touching it might alert the others — or the ship itself.

objects.name: Wall Patterns
objects.description: Intricate geometric patterns covering the walls — art, language, or something else entirely.

then.text: Geometric patterns cover every surface — nested triangles, spiraling fractals, interlocking hexagons. Art? Language? Navigation? Without understanding Choir communication, you can only guess. The patterns shift subtly if you stare too long, responding to the resonance chamber's vibrations.

With the complete translation cipher, the patterns resolve into meaning. It's all three — art, language, and navigation. The walls tell the Choir's history: their creation by the Convergence, their purpose, their travels. There's a note of pride in the patterns. And buried deep, something that might be doubt.

objects.name: Damaged Shuttle
objects.description: A beetle-shaped shuttle with panels removed and visible damage — missing its power cell.

then.text: The middle shuttle is the one in worst shape — panels removed, internal systems exposed. The power cell bay is empty, fuel lines disconnected, navigation offline. But the hull is intact and the launch mechanism works. With the right components, this thing could fly.
The shuttle hums with restored power. Fuel lines connected, navigation initialized. It's ready to fly — straight down to the planet below. This is your ticket off this ship. One-way.

You slot the reactor power cell into the shuttle's empty bay. Systems flicker to life — emergency lighting, basic avionics, status displays. The shuttle has power. But it still needs fuel and navigation to fly.
You reconnect the fuel line, routing propellant from the bay's fuel system to the shuttle's engines. The fuel gauge climbs. Enough for a one-way trip to the planet's surface — barely.

You insert the navigation chip. The shuttle's systems fully initialize — a holographic display shows the planet below, landing zones calculated. The shuttle is repaired. Ready to launch. The bay doors will open on command. This is it.

objects.name: Shuttle Bay Supply Rack
objects.description: A rack of spare parts and supplies for shuttle maintenance.

then.text: Spare parts for shuttle maintenance: replacement panels, sealant tubes, calibration tools. And fuel lines — coiled and labeled. One matches the gauge of the damaged shuttle's disconnected fuel system.
You pull a replacement fuel line from the rack. It's the right gauge for the damaged shuttle — flexible organic tubing that connects the bay's fuel supply to the shuttle's engines.

objects.name: Launch Controls
objects.description: Bay door and launch mechanism controls in a booth overlooking the shuttle bay.

then.text: Launch controls in the overhead booth — bay door operation, launch cradle release, atmospheric containment. From here you could open the bay to space and launch a shuttle. The controls are surprisingly straightforward — the Choir designed for efficiency, not security.

You activate the launch sequence. Alarms blare — bay doors cycling open. The containment field shimmers as atmosphere holds inside the bay while space yawns beyond. The shuttle's cradle unlocks. This is the point of no return. Board the shuttle, and you're heading for the planet.

objects.name: Harvest Station
objects.description: A station for harvesting biological material from the garden's plants.

then.text: Curved cutting tools and collection vessels for harvesting plant materials. The station processes extracts used throughout the ship — medicines, sealants, nutrients. The bio-garden is the ship's pharmacy, its factory, its pantry.

You operate the harvest station, collecting a vial of concentrated plant extract. The liquid is deep green and smells of life — the purest biological substance on this ship. It has restorative properties and is a key ingredient in Choir bio-chemistry.

objects.name: Fibrous Plants
objects.description: Tall, reed-like plants producing strong organic fibers used in ship construction.

then.text: Tall reed-like plants swaying in the nutrient bath. Their stems produce incredibly strong fibers — the same material used in the ship's internal structures. Harvest the fibers and they could reinforce almost anything.
You strip fibers from several reed stems. They're surprisingly strong — like carbon fiber but organic. Wound tightly, they could reinforce a blade, bind components together, or serve as cordage.

objects.name: Carnivorous Plant
objects.description: A large plant with a maw-like flower that tracks your movement.

then.text: The maw-like flower turns to follow you as you move. It's the size of your torso, lined with digestive cilia. The Choir probably grows these as waste disposal or pest control. You're exactly the right size to be 'pest.'
You reach toward the plant experimentally. The maw SNAPS shut, missing your hand by inches. It reopens slowly, cilia waving hungrily. That's a hard no.

objects.name: Brain Interface Terminal
objects.description: One of several terminals around the perimeter for interfacing with the ship's organic brain.

then.text: A terminal for querying the ship's organic brain. Neural cables connect it to the central tank. The interface uses resonance patterns — not keyboards, but vibration-sensitive membranes. Through this terminal, you could access the ship's entire database.

You press your palms against the vibration membranes. Data floods through — too fast, too alien. But you catch fragments: navigation logs, specimen catalogs, maintenance schedules. And resonance frequencies — the crystal harmonics the Choir uses for everything. One crystal in the terminal's output tray contains raw resonance data. You take it.

objects.name: Organic Brain
objects.description: The ship's central computer — a massive brain suspended in translucent fluid, pulsing with thought.

then.text: It fills the tank — folds and ridges of neural tissue, glowing with bio-electric patterns. Neural cables radiate from it in every direction, connecting to every system on the ship. It processes, thinks, dreams. It knows the location of every door, every camera, every specimen. Including you. You can feel it watching, in its alien way.

You try speaking to the brain. Nothing. It doesn't communicate that way. But the vibration membranes on the terminal shimmer in response to your voice — it heard you. It just doesn't care. You're a specimen, not a person. Not to it.

objects.name: Maintenance Drone
objects.description: A small spider-like drone skittering across surfaces, performing automated repairs.

then.text: A spider-like maintenance drone the size of a cat. Eight articulated legs, a cluster of sensor eyes, tool-appendages for welding and cutting. It ignores you completely — you're not a maintenance issue. Not yet.

You grab the drone mid-scuttle. It squeals — a high-pitched mechanical whine — and struggles. You manage to snap off its antenna before it wriggles free and skitters away, broadcasting alarm signals. That'll attract attention.

objects.name: Catwalks
objects.description: Metal catwalks spanning over grinders and acid baths in the waste processing facility.

then.text: Narrow catwalks cross over the machinery below — grinders, acid baths, reprocessing vats. The catwalks connect the engineering section to the hive quarters, a shortcut between decks. It's dangerous, loud, and no one comes here voluntarily. Perfect.

objects.name: Grinders
objects.description: Massive industrial grinders below the catwalks, breaking down waste material.

then.text: The grinders churn constantly, reducing waste material to pulp. The noise is tremendous — the loudest area on the ship. Anything dropped in wouldn't last a second. The good news: the noise here masks everything else. The Curator can't hear you over this din.

objects.name: Observation Instruments
objects.description: Alien instruments for observing and measuring the planet and the harvesting operation.

then.text: Observation instruments trained on the planet below — energy output readings, atmospheric composition, biomass calculations. The Convergence tracks exactly how much life force it's draining. Current extraction: 12.7%. The planet can survive up to about 40% before cascading ecosystem collapse. They're methodical about it. Taking just enough, at just the right rate, to maximize yield.

objects.name: Panoramic Viewport
objects.description: A massive viewport showing the planet below and the Convergence's energy siphon beams descending from orbit.

then.text: The planet fills the viewport — a world of blue oceans and green continents, achingly beautiful. But the energy siphons are visible now: dozens of thin white beams descending from orbital platforms to the surface. Where they touch, the atmosphere yellows. Clouds dissolve. The oceans dim. A world being slowly murdered from orbit. Beautiful and horrifying simultaneously.

objects.name: Shuttle Dashboard
objects.description: The crashed shuttle's instrument panel. Most systems are dead, but some emergency functions still flicker.

then.text: Most instruments are dead — cracked screens, severed cables. But the emergency beacon system still has power, its indicator blinking amber. The navigation display is damaged but partially readable, showing your crash coordinates. If you could signal the shuttle, it might be able to lift off on autopilot... if you're not inside it.

You pry the emergency beacon module from the dashboard. It's self-contained — its own power source, its own transmitter. Press the button and it broadcasts a recall signal to the shuttle's autopilot. One-use only. The shuttle would attempt to launch and fly to the beacon's coordinates. Escape in a box.

objects.name: Emergency Kit
objects.description: A scattered emergency kit — supplies thrown around the cockpit during the crash.

then.text: Emergency supplies scattered during impact: alien first aid components, a Choir-standard signal flare, nutrition packs (empty). The signal flare is still intact — a chemical light source that burns bright enough to be seen from orbit.
You pocket the signal flare. Choir-standard emergency equipment — chemical ignition, burns for about ten minutes at blinding intensity. Useful as a light source, a distraction, or a signal. One shot.

objects.name: Personal Items
objects.description: Items from the Outrider that somehow ended up in the shuttle — a photo, a mug, familiar objects from another life.

then.text: A photograph — you and someone, somewhere warm, smiling. A coffee mug with a chip on the rim. Small things from the Outrider that the Choir must have stored with your other belongings. Evidence of a life before this. You stare at the photo for a long time.

objects.name: Crashed Shuttle Hull
objects.description: The beetle-shaped shuttle half-buried in grey soil, one wing sheared off, smoke still rising.

then.text: The shuttle came down hard — one wing is gone, the hull crumpled on impact. Grey soil piled against the nose where it plowed a furrow across the wasteland. It won't fly again in this state, but the cockpit is relatively intact. Might still have useful supplies inside.

objects.name: Crystal Deposit
objects.description: Crystalline mineral growths at the base of the siphon tower, formed by the Convergence's energy mineralization.

then.text: The ground around the tower base is covered in crystalline mineral deposits — the soil itself transformed by centuries of energy saturation. The minerals shimmer with absorbed planetary energy. They're warm to the touch, faintly radioactive, and unique to harvesting sites.

You chip off a sample of the crystallized mineral. It's warm in your hand, pulsing faintly with stored energy. This mineral has absorbed the Convergence's harvesting energy for years — it might be useful for dampening or redirecting that same energy.

objects.name: Siphon Crystal Spire
objects.description: The base of the massive siphon tower. Energy crackles across its surface. A fragment could be broken off — carefully or otherwise.

then.text: The siphon tower rises hundreds of meters above you — a crystalline spire of compressed energy. Up close, you can see stress fractures where the crystal has grown unevenly. A fragment from this tower would contain raw Convergence energy — incredibly powerful, incredibly dangerous. You could break a piece off with force... or cut one free precisely.

You strike the crystal at a stress fracture with all your strength. A piece breaks free with a DEAFENING crack that echoes across the wasteland. Energy discharges wildly for a moment. Your hands tingle painfully. But you have it — a shard of raw Convergence crystal, pulsing with stolen planetary energy.

You score the crystal along a natural stress line with the reinforced blade, working the cut deeper with patient precision. After several minutes, a clean fragment separates with a soft chime — much quieter than brute force. The crystal pulses in your hand, warm with stolen energy.

objects.name: Scattered Belongings
objects.description: Personal possessions left behind by refugees — clothing, tools, keepsakes, records.

then.text: Scattered across the campsite: clothing sized for four-armed beings, alien tools and utensils, children's toys, data tablets. Among the debris, a journal-like device — a personal record kept by one of the refugees. Its power cell still holds a charge.

You pick up the journal device. It contains a refugee's account of the final days — the Convergence arriving, the evacuation failing, the desperate flight from the city. And buried in the entries, translation notes. This refugee was a linguist, trying to decode Choir communications. Translation cipher fragment three.

objects.name: Supply Crate
objects.description: A sealed supply crate among the refugee camp supplies, still intact.

then.text: A military-standard supply crate, still sealed. The refugee camp was partially supplied by the military before it fell. This crate is marked with symbols that look like climbing equipment and food rations.

You pry the crate open. Inside: climbing pitons designed for four-armed use but adaptable, survival ration packs, and basic medical supplies. The rations are still good — preserved with alien technology that doesn't expire.
You take the climbing pitons — alien metal, light but incredibly strong. They're designed for four hands but work fine with two. Essential for vertical terrain.
You grab the survival rations — compact packs of alien food, nutrient-dense and sealed. They taste like nothing you've ever eaten, but they'll keep you going.

objects.name: Fallen Refugees
objects.description: Skeletons of the planet's former inhabitants — tall, thin, four-armed — lying where they fell during the evacuation.

then.text: Tall, thin skeletons with four arms each. Some clutch bundles to their chests — belongings they refused to leave behind. Others are posed in running stances, caught mid-stride. A family group — two adults, three small ones — huddled together. They never made it out of the camp. The Convergence didn't kill them quickly. It drained their world until nothing could survive.

objects.name: Bioluminescent Fungus
objects.description: A massive mushroom-like organism with a purple-blue bioluminescent cap, producing potent biological extracts.

then.text: A massive fungus with a cap the size of a table, pulsing with purple-blue bioluminescence. The underside drips with a concentrated extract — the fungus's defense mechanism, rich in bio-active compounds. These organisms survived the Convergence's harvest by growing in the rock formation's shadow, where the siphon beams couldn't reach.

You collect the dripping extract in a container. Deep purple, warm, and intensely bio-active — it makes your skin tingle on contact. Potent healing properties and useful as a biochemical reagent. The fungi don't seem to mind the harvest; they regenerate quickly.

objects.name: Fungal Shelter
objects.description: A large fungus hollowed out and used as a crude shelter by survivors. A makeshift door, bedding inside.

then.text: Someone hollowed out this giant fungus and made it home. A crude door, bedding of dried spore material, scratched marks on the inner wall counting days. Whoever lived here survived for a while — the count goes past two hundred. Then stops. A relatively safe haven, but temporary. Everything on this planet is temporary now.

objects.name: Flickering Echoes
objects.description: Ghostly translucent figures and buildings flickering in and out of existence, replaying moments from the past.

then.text: The Echoes flicker like corrupted holograms — buildings shimmer into existence, populated with translucent four-armed figures going about their daily lives. A market. A school. Children playing. Then it stutters, glitches, and you see the same scene overlaid with the moment of destruction: the sky turning yellow, the ground cracking, people running. Past and apocalypse, layered on top of each other.

The echo stabilizer's field steadies the flickering manifestations. They solidify slightly — still translucent, but now stable enough to observe clearly. One figure turns toward you. It sees you. A tall scientist, four arms clutching data tablets, mouth moving. It's trying to tell you something. Without a way to communicate, you can only read its gestures: it points toward the city gates, urgently, repeatedly.

objects.name: Bunker Door
objects.description: A heavy blast door with alien military insignia, partially open. A combination lock secures the inner chamber.

then.text: The outer blast door is forced open — whoever used this bunker didn't bother closing it when they left. But the inner armory door has a combination lock: alien military security, still powered by the bunker's generator. The code isn't obvious.

The combination lock has twelve positions in a hexagonal pattern. Without the code, you'd need to try thousands of combinations. The refugee journal mentioned military dates and protocols — and the bunker defense schematics might contain access procedures.

You enter the code derived from the refugee journal dates and bunker schematics. The lock clicks through its sequence — each position lighting green — and the inner door swings open. Inside: the bunker's armory, still stocked with the planet's last weapons.

You cross-reference the refugee journal's military dates with the notation system on the bunker door. The journal mentions 'the day the sky changed' — a specific date in the alien calendar. Combined with the defense schematics' standard military access protocols, you work out the combination.

objects.name: Weapons Cache
objects.description: Racks of alien military weapons and equipment — the planet's defenders stored their last arsenal here.

then.text: Military equipment from the planet's final defense: sidearms, body armor sized for four-armed soldiers, sensor equipment, and — standing out from the conventional weapons — an echo stabilizer. The previous civilization understood the Echoes and built technology to interact with them.

You take the echo stabilizer — a device that generates a field stabilizing the Convergence's residual energy patterns. With this, you can safely interact with Echoes without them glitching into hostility. It also registers you as a 'memory pattern' rather than a living intruder — useful for getting past the city's automated defenses.

You take an alien sidearm — a compact energy weapon sized for four hands but manageable with two. The charge indicator shows limited power — maybe six shots. Use them wisely. The weapon is loud and powerful, drawing attention but eliminating threats.

objects.name: Command Table
objects.description: A tactical planning table with holographic projectors, showing the planet's last defense plans.

then.text: The holographic projectors still work — a ghostly map of the planet appears above the table. Defense positions marked, siphon tower locations plotted, and a final desperate plan outlined: an assault on the Convergence nexus using a weapon designed to turn the nexus's own energy against itself. They got as far as building prototypes.

You extract the defense schematics from the table's data store. Detailed plans for the nexus assault, weapon prototypes, troop movements. And partial blueprints for the countermeasure weapon — not complete, but a critical piece of the puzzle. Combined with the research lab's full schematics, you'd have everything needed to build it.

objects.name: Equipment Locker
objects.description: A military equipment locker with sensor and safety gear.

then.text: Standard military issue equipment: sensor gear, communication devices (dead), and radiation detection badges. The badges were designed to monitor exposure to Convergence energy — useful for navigating areas of high energy concentration.

You clip a radiation badge to your chest. It immediately starts registering — low background levels from the Convergence's energy field. The badge changes color with exposure: green is safe, yellow is caution, red is dangerous. Currently a steady yellow-green. It'll warn you before you walk into lethal energy zones.

objects.name: Gate Archway
