on_trigger_effects.text: The overcharge device detonates in a burst of resonance static. The Curator recoils, its sensors overwhelmed. Its amber lights flicker wildly.

special_behaviors.description: The Curator has been convinced of your sentience. It ceases hostilities and may assist.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Curator goes still. Its amber sensors dim, then shift — to blue. For the first time, it sees you not as a specimen, but as a person. It lowers its manipulator limbs. It will not hunt you again.

special_behaviors.description: Echoes manifest near the player, causing noise and disturbance.

on_trigger_effects.text: An Echo manifests — a translucent figure stuttering through reality. The disruption sends ripples through the energy field.

special_behaviors.description: The Watcher has detected the player and is restructuring the environment.

on_trigger_effects.text: The Watcher LOCKS onto your position. Crystal grows from the walls, sealing corridors behind you. The geometric shape shifts, its faces reorienting — each one a different sensor, all pointed at you.

win_conditions.description: Escape — 'The Survivor': Flee the system in a shuttle, leaving the planet to its fate. Hollow victory.
Destroy — 'The Sacrifice': Activate the countermeasure at the nexus heart. The planet is saved. You don't make it out.
Sabotage + Escape — 'The Best of Both': Set the countermeasure on a timer, then escape before it detonates. The golden ending.
Signal — 'The Warning': Hijack the transmission array to broadcast Convergence intel and weapon schematics to every inhabited system in range.
Kamikaze — 'The Hammer': Recall the Choir vessel and crash it into the nexus using reactivated orbital defense satellites. Pyrrhic victory — the planet is destroyed too.
Transcendence — 'The Bridge': Interface directly with the Convergence, merging with its intelligence to redirect its hunger. The harvesting stops everywhere. You cease to exist as a person.

lose_conditions.description: Caught by the Curator, an Echo, or a Convergence defense system. Returned to containment (Acts 1-2) or neutralized (Acts 3-5).

lose_conditions.message: The planet shudders one final time. The energy siphons reach critical mass. The surface cracks, continents splitting apart as the Convergence drains the last of the world's energy. The sky burns white. Then — silence. The harvest is complete.
lose_conditions.description: The planet is fully consumed before you can act.

hints.text: Your stasis pod is cracked. Examine it carefully — the glass and fluid may both be useful.
The adjacent pods have specimen log numbers. The lab keypad might respond to a sequence from those logs.
The processing lab has a startup display that cycles through a specific sequence. That pattern might work on the security console.
The ventilation shafts are sized for maintenance drones — but you're small enough to fit. A fine tool could remove the grate.
The data core records contain resonance frequencies used throughout the ship. The bridge lock responds to tonal combinations.
The damaged shuttle in the bay needs three things: a power cell from engineering, a fuel line reconnection, and a navigation chip from the bridge.
The engineering power panel has linked switches — toggling one affects others. Route power to the shuttle bay without triggering the alarm circuit.
The refugee journal mentions dates that were significant to the military. Cross-reference those with the bunker defense schematics for the door code.
The Echoes in the field aren't random — they're replaying their final movements. Watch their paths. They're showing you which way was safe.
The city defenses detect non-native biology. The echo stabilizer from the bunker might make you register as something the city remembers, not something it rejects.
You've found cipher fragments in Acts 1, 2, and 3. The library holds the fourth. With all four, you can read every piece of alien text in this world.
The city power station still works, but can only power three districts at once. Choose carefully — the research district and military quarter may be the most useful.
The weapon vault has alien biometric locks. You might bypass them with a combination of items: the neural tendril from the ship, the echo stabilizer, and a power cell adapter.
The countermeasure needs three components: the primed weapon core, the energy dampener, and a siphon crystal fragment. The ancient blueprint shows the assembly order.

The Curator followed you here. It's a machine that catalogs specimens — prove you're not just a specimen. The ship's black box, your specimen tag, and its own signal device might form an argument it can process.

Multiple paths converge here. The weapon assembly point, the transmission array, the control spire, and the core itself each lead to a different outcome. The prophet's crystal showed you glimpses of all of them.
If you can set the countermeasure on a timer — jury-rig the overcharge device as a detonator — you might have time to reach the escape shaft and get off the planet before it blows.
